propositions.question: What exact GitLab artifact and release line does this record identify?
propositions.status: 18.8.0-ee source revision exact; executed runtime unresolved
propositions.answer: The protected v18.8.0-ee tag identifies Enterprise Edition source revision 1010a9b2b769993080ce8399fd25e77c54e1ad1c, while the 18.8 release page identifies the Developer Flow GA milestone.
propositions.whyItMatters: An exact application source tag does not identify a hosted service, runner executor or model runtime.

propositions.question: How do GitLab.com, Self-Managed and Dedicated applicability differ?
propositions.status: Launch-day and current scopes preserved separately
propositions.answer: The GA announcement said GitLab.com and Self-Managed were available while Dedicated was planned during the 18.8 cycle; current documentation lists all three offerings.
propositions.whyItMatters: Current availability cannot be silently projected to the first day of the 18.8 release line.

propositions.question: What work does GitLab say this background flow can perform?
propositions.answer: Current documentation describes draft merge requests, review-feedback iteration, implementation research, merge-request splitting and conflict resolution, subject to project prerequisites.
propositions.whyItMatters: Documented capability is not observed completion, quality or safety.

propositions.question: Which invocation and execution configuration was effective?
propositions.answer: Offering, trigger path, identity, runner provider, runner executor, sandbox image, agent-config, model and background tool authority remain distinct alternatives.
propositions.whyItMatters: The same product label covers materially different service and execution boundaries.

propositions.question: Whose identity and permissions execute the flow?
propositions.status: 18.8 setting unresolved; current one-time composite identity described
propositions.answer: Current documentation describes a human-plus-service-account composite identity constrained by the more restrictive role and shared project access. The effective 18.8 setting is unknown.
propositions.whyItMatters: The service account, initiator, token type and project intersection define different authority boundaries.

propositions.question: Where and how does the background flow execute?
propositions.status: Runner, executor, package and sandbox unresolved
propositions.answer: GitLab says UI-started flows run through CI/CD, download Duo CLI and connect to the Workflow Service. Hosted and user-managed runners and sandbox-capable and non-capable images remain separate.
propositions.whyItMatters: Runner ownership and configuration determine code, credential, network and isolation boundaries.

propositions.question: Which model served the Developer Flow?
propositions.status: Unknown; release-line flag and rolling defaults separated
propositions.answer: GitLab's 18.8 history identifies a model-selection feature-flag state, not a model. Current defaults may change and selected supported models persist until changed.
propositions.whyItMatters: Application release identity and model runtime identity are independent.

propositions.question: Can a human approve each background tool action?
propositions.status: 18.8 unresolved; no background Always Ask in current 19.3 beta governance
propositions.answer: Current documentation says background tool-governance enforcement arrived only in 19.3 behind a disabled-by-default flag and supports Allow or Deny, not interactive Ask. The 18.8 behavior remains unknown.
propositions.whyItMatters: Later governance cannot be back-projected into the dossier's 18.8 anchor.

propositions.question: Was this exact GitLab record independently evaluated?
propositions.answer: No candidate public evaluation pinned the exact release, offering, runner, executor, model, agent-config, trigger, service identity and approval scope required for admission.
propositions.whyItMatters: Publisher architecture and capability statements must remain attributed rather than treated as observed behavior.

boundaries.note: Attributed official public-source claims only. The exact source release, GA release line, three offerings, runtime configuration, later governance and absent independent evaluation remain explicitly separate.
